design.root_cause: Always On Top uses the current foreground HWND for both pin/unpin and opacity hotkeys without filtering shell desktop hosts. ProcessCommand only checks game mode and the user exclusion list, and ResolveTransparencyTargetWindow only checks IsPinned(window). When the desktop background (Progman/WorkerW) is foreground, the module pins that shell window and StepWindowTransparency then applies WS_EX_LAYERED alpha directly to it, dimming the desktop and icons.
evidence: The issue repro is exactly: focus the desktop, press the Always On Top activation shortcut, then press the opacity shortcuts; the desktop becomes darker.
src/modules/alwaysontop/AlwaysOnTop/AlwaysOnTop.cpp routes both hotkey paths to GetForegroundWindow() and never rejects Program Manager / WorkerW before ProcessCommand or StepWindowTransparency.
ResolveTransparencyTargetWindow returns the pinned window unchanged once IsPinned(window) is true.
src/common/utils/window.h already provides is_system_window(...) for desktop/taskbar classes including Progman, WorkerW, Shell_TrayWnd, and SysListView32.

affected_files.purpose: Reject shell desktop/taskbar windows before pinning, tracking, or changing transparency.
Turn the existing weak system-window tests into deterministic assertions that the helper treats desktop/shell windows as system windows and ordinary windows as non-system windows.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Any foreground window that is not user-excluded can be pinned, including Progman/WorkerW and other shell-owned windows.
implementation_steps.change: Add a small helper that reads the foreground window class name and calls is_system_window(...); early-return from ProcessCommand when the target is the desktop/taskbar/shell host.
tests: Manual desktop-background repro should stop at the pin step.
Existing ordinary pin/unpin behavior on normal app windows must remain unchanged.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Once a shell window is pinned (or already carries the pinned property), opacity changes and startup recovery can continue to act on it.
implementation_steps.change: Use the same shell-window guard in ResolveTransparencyTargetWindow and while enumerating startup-tracked pinned windows, so stale shell properties are ignored and transparency never applies to desktop/taskbar surfaces.
tests: Restart Always On Top after pinning a normal window and verify tracked windows still recover.
Opacity hotkeys on the desktop should do nothing even if the desktop had been foreground previously.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The existing tests only assert that is_system_window does not crash; they do not lock in true/false behavior that Always On Top can rely on.
implementation_steps.change: Strengthen the desktop/shell helper tests to assert true for GetDesktopWindow()/GetShellWindow() and false for a normal synthetic top-level test window.
tests: Keep existing Always On Top startup/manual verification green.

verify: Build the Always On Top module and UnitTests-CommonUtils using the repo build scripts.
Run the strengthened UnitTests-CommonUtils window tests.
Manual repro: click the desktop background, press the Always On Top activation shortcut, then the opacity up/down shortcuts; confirm nothing about the desktop appearance changes.
Manual regression: pin a normal app window, adjust opacity up/down, unpin it, and confirm transparency and border behavior still work as before.
risks: Some shell-owned windows share generic classes, so the guard must stay narrowly scoped to windows that really should never be pinned or alpha-adjusted.
Startup recovery of already-pinned windows must not stop restoring legitimate app windows.
System menu integration should continue to work for normal windows even after adding shell filtering.
alternatives: Blocking only the opacity hotkeys would still let users pin Program Manager and leave an invalid pinned state behind.
Special-casing only Progman misses WorkerW / taskbar / shell listview hosts that also should not be touched.
Trying to restore the desktop alpha after the fact is less safe than refusing to mutate shell windows in the first place.
